title: Can AI Reviewers See Your Efforts to Improve Your Paper? A Large-Scale Study of Paper Revision Trajectories
abstract: arXiv:2611.02244v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI reviewers are increasingly used to assess scientific manuscripts, yet it remains unclear whether their judgments reflect the improvements authors make through revision. We investigate this question using PaperTrajectory-2026, the 2026 release of PaperTrajectory, a dataset of 6,959 paper trajectories across five AI conferences, with automatic annotations of changes along 14 dimensions and separate judgments of overall quality. The annotations show that major improvements emphasize empirical evidence and framing, while later revisions tend toward incremental improvement. Using independent assessments of manuscript versions from eight AI reviewers, we examine whether annotated major improvements receive higher scores, which revision dimensions are associated with score changes, and whether user opinions can outweigh observed revision gains. Every reviewer leaves scores unchanged on most major improvements, and agreement on the direction

translated_title: AI审稿人能看到你改进论文的努力吗？关于论文修改轨迹的大规模研究
translated_abstract: AI审稿人正被越来越多地用于评估科学论文手稿，然而其评判是否能反映作者通过修改所做出的改进，这一问题尚不清楚。我们使用PaperTrajectory-2026数据集研究这一问题——该数据集是PaperTrajectory的2026年版本，涵盖五个AI会议的6,959篇论文轨迹，并对14个维度上的变化进行了自动标注，同时提供了对整体质量的独立评判。标注结果显示，重大改进主要集中在实证证据和论文定位方面，而后期的修改往往趋向于渐进式提升。通过使用八位AI审稿人对论文不同版本进行独立评估，我们检验了以下问题：被标注为重大改进的部分是否能获得更高分数、哪些修改维度与分数变化相关，以及用户意见是否能够超越观察到的修改收益。研究发现，每位AI审稿人在大多数重大改进上都保持分数不变，并且（原文此处截断）
tldr: 研究发现AI审稿人在论文评审中往往无法识别作者通过修改做出的重大改进，对大多数标注确认的重大修改保持评分不变，这揭示了AI评审系统在评估论文改进方面的严重局限性。
en_tdlr: AI reviewers largely fail to recognize authors' major improvements made during paper revision, leaving scores unchanged on most confirmed significant changes, revealing critical limitations of AI-based peer review in assessing manuscript revisions.
